subskill: Integers in one solution set but not another
prompt:
-17 ≤ -9 - 2x < 9
5x - 2k > 4
In the inequalities above, k is a constant. Exactly 4 integers satisfy the first inequality and fail to satisfy the second. What is the least possible integer value of k?
explanation: First inequality: adding 9 gives -8 ≤ -2x < 18, and dividing by -2 reverses both signs: 4 ≥ x > -9. So its integer solutions are -8, -7, ..., 4; the end 4 IS included (it came from ≤) and -9 is NOT (it came from <). Second inequality: 5x > 2k + 4, so x > (2k + 4)/5. An integer fails the second inequality exactly when x ≤ (2k + 4)/5. So the integers that satisfy the first but fail the second run upward from -8 to the greatest integer not above (2k + 4)/5. For exactly 4 of them they must be -8, -7, -6, -5: -5 ≤ (2k + 4)/5 < -4. Multiplying by 5: -25 ≤ 2k + 4 < -20, so -29 ≤ 2k < -24, that is, -14.5 ≤ k < -12. The integer values are -14 and -13, and the least is -14. Choice -17 treats -9 as a solution of the first inequality, so the four integers would be -9, -8, -7, -6. Choice -29 drops the 2 in 2k (solving 5x - k > 4). Choice 13 moves 2k to the other side with the wrong sign, x > (4 - 2k)/5.
solve: const cnt=(k,hiIn,mode)=>{let n=0; for (let x=-150;x<=150;x++){ const t=-9-2*x; const P=(-17<=t)&&(hiIn?t<=9:t<9); let Q=5*x-2*k>4; if(mode==='slip') Q=5*x+2*k>4; if(mode==='nok') Q=5*x-k>4; if(P&&!Q) n++; } return n;}; const L=(hiIn,mode)=>{ for (let k=-300;k<=300;k++) if (cnt(k,hiIn,mode)===4) return k; return null; }; return L(false,'');
